PAPERS.title: Cause-specific hospital admissions associated with short-term PM2.5 exposure: a multicountry time-series analysis
PAPERS.pm: Daily ambient PM2.5 (community-level), lags to 21 days
PAPERS.geo: Multi-country (Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, New Zealand, Taiwan)
PAPERS.n: 346.5 million admissions from 949 communities in six countries/territories, 2000-2019; quasi-Poisson time series pooled by meta-analysis. Per 10 ug/m3, all-cause admissions RR 1.080 (1.074-1.086), with effects persisting to 21 days. Malignant neoplasms (1.108, 1.094-1.123), mental disorders (1.100) and nervous system disease (1.085) all exceed respiratory (1.067, 1.060-1.074). Attributable fraction against the WHO daily 15 ug/m3 fell from 8.9% (2000-09) to 3.9% (2010-19). Limitation: a 21-day distributed lag on cancer admissions invites harvesting and scheduling artefacts - an elective oncology admission is not an acute PM event - and heterogeneity across countries is described as substantial but the pooled RR is reported without it. Relevance: high - the long-lag, non-respiratory signal argues for continuous rather than episodic sensing.

PAPERS.title: Carbonaceous Components Underlying Wildfire Smoke PM2.5-Associated Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias in Older US Adults
PAPERS.pm: Annual smoke vs non-smoke PM2.5 and smoke EC/OC (high-resolution model)
PAPERS.n: 39.7 million fee-for-service Medicare beneficiaries, 2005-2019, 8.4 million incident ADRD cases; stratified Cox. Per 1 ug/m3, smoke PM2.5 HR 1.029 (1.024-1.035) for ADRD and 1.015 (1.005-1.026) for AD; the smoke carbonaceous fraction HR 1.090 (1.077-1.103) for ADRD. Per IQR the non-smoke association is larger (ADRD 1.048 vs 1.009) because smoke exposure contrast is narrow. Attributable: 11,142 ADRD cases/year. Limitation: preprint; annual smoke partitioning is model-derived and its error is not propagated, and claims-based incident dementia carries diagnostic-intensity confounding that tracks rurality and fire-prone regions. Relevance: high - argues for composition-resolved smoke metrics that optical LCS cannot supply without co-located carbon measurement.

PAPERS.title: Acute cardiovascular mortality risks from PM2.5 and its chemical components in an industrial valley city: evidence from Lanzhou, China
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5; random-forest-predicted components (PAHs, metals, ions)
PAPERS.n: 69,669 CVD deaths, 2015-2023. PM2.5 lag 0: excess risk 2.06% per 10 ug/m3 (0.66-3.48%), larger in men and under-65s. qgcomp/WQS attribute risk to PAHs and Tl/Pb/Mn in traffic-dominated Chengguan, and to nitrate/chloride/sulfate and PAHs in industrial Xigu. Limitation: components are not measured but predicted by a random forest with r>0.70, so the mixture weights inherit the predictor set of that model - district contrasts may reflect which inputs drove the prediction rather than toxicity. Relevance: moderate - a valley inversion city where source-specific nodes would test exactly these district contrasts.

PAPERS.title: Acute Respiratory Impacts of Fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5) in Kinshasa: Epidemiological Evidence and Pulmonological Implications
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5 from PurpleAir and QuantAQ Modulair sensors plus bias-corrected GEOS-CF
PAPERS.n: 13,049 adult admissions at one hospital, 2018-2022; mean daily PM2.5 46-50 ug/m3. Per 10 ug/m3 over lag 0-5, adjusted OR 1.01 (1.00-1.03), strongest at 35-64 years and in Tshangu and Funa. Limitation: a single-hospital catchment against a city-wide exposure series, and an estimate whose lower bound sits on the null; the sensor and model fusion step is described but its validation against any reference in Kinshasa is not. Relevance: high - one of the first African health analyses whose exposure series is built on low-cost sensors, which makes the uncorrected sensor error the main threat to the inference.

PAPERS.title: Explainable spatiotemporal Graph Neural Networks: Multi-City PM2.5 forecasting in Bangladesh with geographic graph topology validation
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5, 12-city network, 1-3 day forecasts
PAPERS.n: Graph-diffusion GRU on four years of daily multi-source data at 12 cities. Up to 3-day lead: MAE 8.85 ug/m3, R2 0.666, beating non-graph baselines (FDR-corrected Diebold-Mariano p<0.001) and DCRNN when pooled across horizons. The useful result is negative for complexity: a fixed distance-adjacency graph beat adaptive, wind-informed and hybrid graphs, and occlusion-based influence tracked geographic adjacency (r=0.928). Limitation: 12 nodes is too sparse to discriminate graph topologies - transport structure that matters at 10-50 km scale cannot be resolved by stations hundreds of km apart. Relevance: high - a direct test of what graph priors a denser LCS network would need before learned adjacency pays off.

PAPERS.title: Comparison of respirable dust concentrations between gravimetric weighing and real-time dust monitoring equipment in non-mining industries
PAPERS.pm: Respirable dust: Nanozen DustCount 9000 optical vs its built-in filter cassette
PAPERS.n: 20 paired task-based stationary samples at 11 industrial sites. No significant difference between gravimetric and raw real-time (Wilcoxon p=0.067) or density-adjusted (p=0.277); proportional bias grew with concentration but was absent below 1 mg/m3 (R2 0.06 and 0.02). Limitation: n=20, and the gravimetric reference is the instrument's own cassette downstream of the same inlet, so inlet losses and size-selection error are shared and invisible to the comparison; Wilcoxon non-significance at n=20 is not agreement. Relevance: moderate - the 1 mg/m3 cut is a usable operating limit, and the shared-inlet design is a pattern to avoid in LCS co-location.

PAPERS.title: Fusion-DeepRSM for Satellite-Derived PM2.5 Estimation and Precursor Sensitivity Prediction
PAPERS.pm: Gridded PM2.5 from CTM + multisource satellite + ground fusion
PAPERS.n: Observation-constrained deep response-surface model fusing CTM runs, satellite products and ground PM2.5. R2 0.872, RMSE 11.82 ug/m3, and a 4.13 ug/m3 reduction in rural overestimation, the known failure of station-trained ML. It also returns precursor-PM2.5 response surfaces: for 2020-2023, meteorology offset part of emission-driven improvement (+1.2 vs -1.8 ug/m3), and precursor change drove the Feb 2023 BTH rebound. Limitation: validation against stations that are themselves inputs; the rural bias correction is quantified on a CTM testbed, not against independent rural monitors - exactly where LCS would be needed. Relevance: high - a fusion architecture into which rural sensor nodes would slot as the missing constraint.

PAPERS.title: Spatiotemporal variation of PM2.5 and its relationship with vegetation cover and meteorological factors during spring (2016-2022) in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
PAPERS.pm: Spring PM2.5 from 16 regulatory stations; fractional vegetation cover
PAPERS.n: 16 stations, spring 2016-2022: seasonal mean PM2.5 ranged from 94.6 (2018) to 55.0 ug/m3 (2020), highest in southern and central Riyadh. Meteorological correlations were non-significant; the vegetation-PM2.5 inverse association reached significance in one year only (rho=-0.539, p=0.031, n=16). Limitation: n=16 Spearman correlations per year cannot separate vegetation from land use, and dust events dominate spring variance; the one significant year out of seven is consistent with chance. Relevance: low-moderate - documents a dust-dominated regime where optical sensors' coarse-mode bias would govern any network.

PAPERS.title: Vertical distribution of pollution trapped by wintertime surface inversions in Fairbanks, Alaska, during the ALPACA experiment
PAPERS.pm: Vertical trace-gas profiles (LP-DOAS) with 1-D chemistry-transport model
PAPERS.n: Long-path DOAS profiles during ALPACA 2022 resolve polluted surface layers 20-40 m deep persisting for days, with SO2 to 35 ppb, NO2 60 ppb, HONO 2.5 ppb, HCHO 7 ppb and depleted ozone. PACT-1D, with mixing parameterised from surface temperature gradient and wind, reproduces the profiles and gives a 1-4 h residence time. Limitation: gas-phase only - particulate profiles, the health-relevant quantity in Fairbanks, are not retrieved - and one winter at one city. Relevance: high for siting - a 20-40 m layer means a node on a rooftop and one at breathing height sample different air masses under inversions.

PAPERS.title: Simultaneous measurements of gas- and aerosol-phase water-soluble organic nitrogen in the winter urban atmosphere of Chengdu, China
PAPERS.pm: Gas- and particle-phase WSON and amines; aerosol liquid water content
PAPERS.n: Winter urban campaign: particulate WSON 2.3+/-1.4 ugN/m3, twice gaseous, rising with PM2.5; particle fraction 0.70+/-0.14. WSON partitions into organic phase under warm-dry and into aerosol liquid water under cold-humid conditions; amines are mainly gaseous but shift to particles as aminium sulfate/nitrate during episodes. ALWC dominated partitioning over T, RH and pH; NH4NO3 was the main ALWC contributor. Limitation: one site, one season, and thermodynamic S-curve confirmation is model-on-model. Relevance: moderate - ALWC is precisely what inflates optical PM readings at high RH, so the nitrate-ALWC link is a calibration covariate as well as a chemistry result.

PAPERS.title: Oxidative Potential and Elemental Fingerprints of Urban and Suburban Particulate Matter in Turin
PAPERS.pm: PM10 oxidative potential (ascorbic acid assay); total and bioaccessible metals
PAPERS.n: 32 PM10 filters (urban traffic vs rural background, 2020-2021, min and max days of four months). Urban OP-AA 0.12-0.60 vs suburban 0.10-0.38 nmol AA/min/m3; Cu was the most active single metal. Total and phosphate-buffer bioaccessible metal fractions were compared. Limitation: filters were selected at monthly concentration extremes, so OP-mass relationships are inflated by design, and n=32 cannot support source attribution of OP. Relevance: low-moderate - OP remains unmeasurable by optical nodes; the Cu dominance points to brake-wear tracers as the practical proxy.

PAPERS.title: Scale-Dependent Effects of Three-Dimensional Urban Vegetation on Land Surface Temperature and Air Pollutants: Synergy and Trade-Off Zones in Guangzhou, China
PAPERS.pm: 1 km gridded PM2.5, O3, NO2; layered vegetation volume
PAPERS.n: Field LAI in 570 quadrats showed MODIS LAI is uninformative (r=0.15), so 3-D greenness was proxied by canopy height x tree cover. MGWR at 1-5 km: one SD of vegetation volume associated with 1.3 C lower LST, 0.30 ug/m3 lower PM2.5 and 1.3 ug/m3 lower NO2; O3 null citywide with offsetting local responses. Limitation: PM2.5 is a 1 km product whose own predictors include land cover, so the vegetation coefficient is partly the model reading its inputs back. Relevance: low-moderate - 0.3 ug/m3 is below the error floor of any LCS network, which is itself the point.

PAPERS.title: Longitudinal personal environmental exposure and Streptococcus pneumoniae colonisation in a cohort of children 5-14 years old in rural Gambia
PAPERS.pm: Personal 24-h PM2.5 and CO monitors, repeated (8 visits)
PAPERS.n: 134 children aged 5-14, 554 visits with paired personal exposure and culture. Geometric mean personal PM2.5 12.6 ug/m3 (12.2-13.1), CO 0.16 ppm; colonisation 39.7%. Neither PM2.5 nor CO was associated with colonisation after adjustment, including in within/between-child decomposition; between-child temperature was inversely associated (OR 0.74, 0.56-0.98). Limitation: personal PM2.5 of 12.6 ug/m3 in solid-fuel households is implausibly low for wood-smoke exposure and suggests the monitor or its wear compliance under-captured cooking peaks; a null under that exposure contrast is uninformative. Relevance: high - a clear case where personal-monitor validation, not the epidemiology, decides the result.

PAPERS.title: Associations of Green Space and Air Pollution Mixture with Heterogeneous Biological Aging Patterns
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5, PM10, SO2, O3 mixture (WQS); 500 m NDVI
PAPERS.n: 11,760 adults aged 20-65 with repeated measures, accelerated longitudinal design; three BAA trajectories. Pollution mixture OR 1.16 (1.08-1.24) for accelerated-aging membership, driven mainly by O3 and PM10; NDVI OR 0.84 (0.75-0.95), 25% of which was mediated through lower pollution. Limitation: trajectories differ in level, not slope, so the design measures cross-sectional BAA differences dressed as trajectories; exposure contrast within one city is narrow and residential NDVI is strongly SES-patterned. Relevance: moderate - the narrow within-city contrast is the case for intra-urban sensor density. Held from the 9 Oct issue.

PAPERS.title: Air Pollution and Neurovascular Health in Pakistan: An Emerging Public Health Crisis in South Asia - A Narrative Review
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5, PM10, UFP (literature)
PAPERS.n: Narrative synthesis of mechanisms - systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, BBB disruption, microglial activation, prothrombotic change - linking particulate exposure to ischaemic and haemorrhagic stroke and small-vessel disease, with the observation that Pakistan has no longitudinal, biomarker or exposure-linked stroke surveillance data. Limitation: no search strategy, no new data, no quantitative synthesis; the gap statement is the contribution. Relevance: low-moderate - a call for registry-linked exposure that presupposes the monitoring network Pakistan does not have.

PAPERS.title: Geochemical Characteristics of the Pollution of Snow Cover with Aerosols in an Industrial Center (Pavlodar, North-Eastern Kazakhstan)
PAPERS.pm: Elemental composition of snow-cover solid fraction (ICP-MS)
PAPERS.n: 55 snow samples across industrial, buffer, non-industrial and background zones. Pb exceeded background 2-100-fold, with Pb, Sr and V peaking in industrial and buffer zones; PC1 loaded on rare-earth elements. Limitation: snowpack integrates wet and dry deposition over an unknown accumulation period, so it is a deposition map, not an air concentration map, and cannot be converted to inhalation exposure. Relevance: low - useful as a cheap spatial prior for siting composition samplers where no network exists.

PAPERS.title: A nested case-control study of air pollution and congenital heart defects via circulating proteins
PAPERS.pm: Periconception PM2.5, PM10, NO2; maternal and cord serum proteomics
PAPERS.n: Maternal periconception PM2.5, PM10 and NO2 were each associated with CHD, NO2 most strongly; supervised sparse PLS identified pollutant-specific protein signatures in maternal and umbilical cord serum that tracked exposure and CHD, implicating FGF-4, VEGF-D, MSP and angiogenin. Limitation: the abstract gives no effect sizes or n; cord serum is sampled at delivery, months after cardiogenesis, so a cord-protein signature cannot be the mechanism of a first-trimester malformation, and supervised signature selection on the same outcome inflates association. Relevance: moderate - periconception exposure windows are short, which favours high-resolution residential estimates. Held from the 9 Oct issue.

PAPERS.title: Differential toxicity of water- and DMSO-extractable PM2.5 fractions in human alveolar organoids
PAPERS.pm: Water- vs DMSO-extractable PM2.5 fractions
PAPERS.endpoint: Organoid morphology, ROS, cell death, AT2/AT1 ratio
PAPERS.n: Human alveolar organoids exposed to extracted PM2.5 showed dose- and time-dependent morphological damage, more severe for the DMSO-extractable (organic) fraction, with ROS rise, cell death and a sustained fall in AT2 cells plus a small AT1 increase suggesting AT2-to-AT1 transdifferentiation. Limitation: doses are not reported in deposited-mass terms, so relevance to ambient exposure is unknowable, and extraction solvents select chemistry rather than particles. Relevance: low - model development. Held from the 9 Oct issue.

PAPERS.title: Are Short-Term Increases in PM2.5 Linked to Respiratory Hospitalizations in IPF?
PAPERS.pm: Short-term PM2.5
PAPERS.n: No abstract in PubMed, Europe PMC or Semantic Scholar at harvest; the title format suggests a research letter on short-term PM2.5 and respiratory admissions in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Recorded for coverage only - no result can be summarised, and none is inferred. Relevance: moderate if positive, because IPF is a small, identifiable cohort for which personal or home-sensor exposure is feasible.

PAPERS.title: Oxidative toxicity and cytotoxicity of toluene combustion soot particles mediated by their microstructure
PAPERS.pm: Laboratory toluene-flame soot
PAPERS.n: No abstract retrievable at harvest. From the title: soot generated from toluene combustion, with oxidative potential and cytotoxicity attributed to particle microstructure (likely graphitisation/nanostructure order). Recorded for coverage; no result is inferred. Relevance: low-moderate - if microstructure rather than mass sets toxicity, mass-based optical sensing misses a toxicity axis entirely.

PAPERS.title: Transport-aware spatiotemporal deep learning for accurate PM10 forecasts during dust storms
PAPERS.pm: PM10 during dust storms
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates a spatiotemporal deep-learning PM10 forecaster with explicit transport awareness, targeted at dust storms where station-only models lag the plume. Recorded for coverage; no metric is inferred. Relevance: moderate - upwind sensor placement is the obvious data complement to transport-aware models.

PAPERS.title: Air Quality Impacts of Post-monsoon Crop Residue Burning in Northern India Based on Regional and Global Emission Inventories
PAPERS.pm: Modelled PM2.5 from crop-residue burning
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates a comparison of regional and global emission inventories for post-monsoon crop-residue burning and the resulting air-quality impact in northern India. Recorded for coverage. Relevance: moderate - inventory spread is the dominant uncertainty in Indo-Gangetic smoke attribution, and dense sensors are the observational constraint that could arbitrate between inventories.

PAPERS.title: From rapid decline to slower improvement: Decadal nonlinear evolution and regional predictive associations of PM2.5 in China (2015-2024)
PAPERS.pm: Ambient PM2.5 trends, 2015-2024
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates a nonlinear trend analysis of Chinese PM2.5 showing deceleration of the post-2015 decline and regional predictors. Recorded for coverage. Relevance: low-moderate - slower improvement means smaller year-on-year signals, which raises the bar on sensor drift control for trend detection.

PAPERS.title: Health and economic benefits of air quality improvements in France through diverse net-zero transition scenarios by 2050
PAPERS.pm: Scenario-modelled PM2.5 and co-pollutants to 2050
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates a health-impact and economic assessment of air-quality co-benefits under several French net-zero pathways to 2050. Recorded for coverage; no estimate is inferred. Relevance: low - scenario work, but it fixes the concentration ranges a future network would need to resolve.
